question: Who was the founder of the Satavahana dynasty in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Simuka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The founder of the Satavahana dynasty was Simuka.
 
• The Satavahanas established their independent rule after the decline of the Mauryas.
 
• Satavahanas ruled over parts of western and central India.
 
• They were also known as the Andhras.
 
• The Puranas and inscriptions remain important sources for the history of Satavahanas.
 
• Important inscriptions:
 
 
• The Nasik and Nanaghad inscriptions throw much light on the reign of Gautamiputra Satakarni. 
 
 
 
• Satvahana rulers worshipped a large number of Vaishnava gods such as Krishna, Vasudeva, and others.
 
• The official language of the Satavahanas was Prakrit.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The first king and founder of the Satavahana dynasty was Simuka.
 
• The assumed the title of Dakshinapatha Pati.
 
• Important rulers of Satavahana dynasty:
 
 
• Simuka
 
• Shatakarni
 
• Hala
 
• Gowtami Putra Satakarni
 
• Vashishta Putra Pulamavi
 
• Yagna Sri Satakarni
 
 
 
• The administration of Satavahana dynasty was entirely based on Shastras and it had following structure:
 
 
• Rajan or the king who was the ruler
 
• Princes or Rajas who had their names inscribed on coins
 
• Maharathis who had the power of granting villages and also have the privilege of maintaining marital relations with ruling family
 
• Mahasenapati
 
• Mahatalavara
